newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica petrol gasoline rise 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica petrol gasoline rise 15 percent.

text.p: Fuel-price increases of 15 percent took effect in Costa Rica on Friday as part of a government plan to ease the country's $3.5 billion internal debt.
President Jose Maria Figueres had announced the hike in government-controlled fuel prices on Dec. 16.
The government is applying a selective new tax on petroleum consumption, the Costa Rican Petroleum Refinery said in a news release.

The new prices are likely to result in a 12 percent increase in home electricity costs and a 13 percent increase in residential water bills, Leonel Fonseca, director of the Public Services Regulatory Authority, told reporters.
In addition, public transportation costs will rise 20 percent as of Monday, Fonseca said.
Fonseca said bus drivers have been asking for an increase in government-controlled fares since last year and that the increase was granted because of the increase in fuel prices.
Premium gasoline has gone up to the equivalent of $0.54 per liter ($2.03 per U.S. gallon) while regular gasoline rose to $0.51 per liter ($1.93 per U.S. gallon).
Diesel, the primary fuel for buses and trucks, rose to $0.36 per liter ($1.35 per U.S. gallon).
Prices also rose for others fuels such as kerosene.
